title: UKPNP AND SKHRC STAGE PROTEST OUTSIDE UN GENEVA OVER AZAD KASHMIR CRACKDOWN DURING UNHRC 62ND SESSION IN GENEVA
subtitle: Rights organizations submit urgent memorandum to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, demanding an independent OHCHR fact-finding mission and an end to the communications siege.

body.text: GENEVA, June 26, 2026 — Representatives of the United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) and the Swiss Kashmir Human Rights Commission (SKHRC) staged a high-profile demonstration outside the United Nations headquarters in Geneva on Wednesday, protesting against reported state violence and human rights abuses in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir.

The demonstration brought together members of the Kashmiri diaspora alongside Baloch and Pashtun rights activists. Organizers officially submitted an urgent memorandum addressed to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), and the UN Security Council, calling for immediate global intervention to halt kinetic operations against civil rights movements in the region.

body.caption: Demonstrators gathered outside the UN Palais des Nations in Geneva protesting human rights conditions in Azad Kashmir.

body.text: Addressing the crowd in Geneva, UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri criticized the government's response to peaceful advocacy: "The Joint Awami Action Committee has conducted a peaceful movement for three years, consistently advocating for negotiations and democratic rights. It is tragic that while authorities speak of peace globally, they deploy direct gunfire against civilians in their own periphery."

The UKPNP reiterated that the international community cannot remain silent while fundamental rights, including the rights to life, assembly, and free expression, are systematically restricted, warning that lasting regional stability depends on democratic engagement and strict adherence to international law.

body.caption: UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri addressing activists and media representatives at UN Geneva.

body.text: Key Issues Highlighted in the UN Memorandum

During the rally outside the Palais des Nations, protest led by UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri outlined severe concerns regarding security deployments and administrative blockades in Poonch, Kotli, Muzaffarabad, Sudhnuti, and surrounding districts:

items: Civilian Fatalities Under Fire: Allegations that external paramilitary formations, including Rangers, the Frontier Constabulary (FC) and Punjab Constabulary, opened live fire on unarmed public gatherings, resulting in over 24 verified civilian deaths across Rawalakot, Kotli, and neighboring areas.

Proscription of Civic Movement: The use of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) of 2014 to declare the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a broad movement advocating for fair electricity tariffs and subsidized wheat flour, a "terrorist organization" to justify security operations.

Collective Punishment and Blackouts: A complete suspension of cellular networks, broadband internet, and local press access, combined with road blockades that rights groups claim have created artificial shortages of food, fuel, and medical supplies.

Medical Facilities Affected: Reports that security personnel occupied local triage centers and medical hubs, obstructing wounded demonstrators, pregnant women, and elderly citizens from receiving critical care.

body.caption: Kashmiri, Baloch, and Pashtun diaspora leaders holding banners advocating for human rights and press freedom.

body.text: Demands Submitted to the United Nations
The memorandum officially calls upon the United Nations and its affiliated human rights mechanisms to execute the following steps:

items: OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission: Deploy an independent, international fact-finding mission to investigate massacres, unlawful killings, and allegations of enforced disappearances in Rawalakot and Kotli.
Withdrawal of Paramilitary Troops: Order the immediate withdrawal of heavy external paramilitary units from civilian population centers and healthcare facilities.
Restoration of Telecommunications: Force the immediate lifting of all digital and communication blackouts across Azad Kashmir.
Decriminalization of Dissent: Rescind the anti-terror notification proscribing the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and release all arbitrarily detained activists.

body.text: The demonstration was attended by a broad delegation of organizational leaders, international observers, human rights defenders, media representatives, and diaspora activists, including: The protest was led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Chairman of United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP); other keynote speakers included Mr. Mahmood Ahmed Kashmiri, Chairman of Jammu Kashmir National Independence Alliance (JKNIA); Dr. Chongsi Ayeah Joseph, President & Chief Executive of Centre for Human Rights and Peace Advocacy; Fazal Rehman Afridi, President of IRESK - Khyber Institute for Research & Strategic Studies; Jamil Maqsood, President of Foreign Affairs Committee UKPNP; Mr. Sardar Amjad Yousaf, President of Europe Zone UKPNP; Asif Abbas, General Secretary of Europe Zone UKPNP; Mr. Tika Khan Tahir, Central Secretary Information UKPNP; Mr. Sajid Hussain, Secretary Information Europe Zone UKPNP; Mr. Yasar Arfat Hussain Begum, Secretary Finance Europe Zone UKPNP; Mr. Abdul Shafiq Habegger, President of Swiss Kashmir Human Rights Commission; Mr. Naveed Khan, President of Leeds Unit UKPNP; Mr. Aqeel Ahmad, President of UKPNP Belgium; Kamran Ayub, President of UKPNP Italy. Among participants, activists, and Kashmiri diaspora were Mr. Raja Muhammad Sheraz Khan; Mr. Abdul Rehman Khursheed; Mr. Qamar Khalil; Mr. Noyal Malik; Mr. Hamza Shakeel; Mr. Majid Bashir; Aamir Ali; Abdul Waheed Khan; Muhammed Ilyas Shahid; Mohammad Younas Khan (Journalist); Bilal Baloch; alongside several other human rights defenders and civil society members.
